Ingenia Ends Warburg Pincus's Access as AVID Matches Offer
By Stuart Condie

SYDNEY--Australia's Ingenia Communities terminated Warburg Pincus's due diligence access after AVID Properties matched the New York-based private-equity group's offer for the retirement-village operator.
ASX-listed Ingenia on Monday said it closed its books to Warburg Pincus after L&G-controlled AVID raised its all-cash offer to 5.45 Australian dollars a share, equivalent to US$3.83.
The offer excludes any distribution for the six months through December up to A$0.05 a share, making it effectively worth A$5.50 a share.

Ingenia said that was equal or superior to last week's offer from Warburg Pincus. That offer had been a response to a A$5.35-a-share proposal by AVID, which had persuaded Ingenia's board to firm up discussions by entering into a process deed.
"The AVID process deed remains on foot and Ingenia has terminated Warburg Pincus's access to Ingenia's due diligence," Ingenia said in a statement.
AVID is a subsidiary of Proprium Capital Partners, which is 75% owned by U.K.-listed asset manager L&G.
